extracted.intended_audience: writers, students, critics, and readers interested in the genre of magical realism across literature, visual art, film, and games
extracted.subtask_description: Identify and apply the distinctive characteristics that define magical realism (how to present the marvelous within realistic settings, and how it differs from surrealism, fabulism, fantasy, and related modes) across literary and visual media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of fantastical elements into everyday reality
rubrics_metrics.description: Fantastic (magical) elements appear as part of everyday reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fantastic is presented as embedded in ordinary life (often functioning, in examples given, as saviors of the human against conformism, evil and totalitarianism). Narration often retains objective traits of traditional realism even while ordinary life contains marvels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defamiliarization, myth/legend, and supplementation rather than mimetic empiricism
rubrics_metrics.description: Magic realism encompasses terms such as 'myth/legend', 'fantastic/supplementation', 'defamiliarization', 'mysticism/magic', 'meta-narration', 'open-ended/expansive romanticism', and 'imagination/negative capability' as opposed to realism's 'mimetic', 'empiricism/logic', 'narration', 'closure-ridden/reductive naturalism', and 'rationalization/cause and effect'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize mythic or legendary resonances, estrangement/defamiliarization of the everyday, openness and imaginative scope rather than strict cause-and-effect explanation or reductive closure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordinariness of the magical (not presented as dream/psychological experience)
rubrics_metrics.description: Magical realism rarely presents the extraordinary as a dream or psychological experience; the ordinariness of magical realism's magic relies on its accepted and unquestioned position in tangible and material reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid framing marvels as merely inner-psychic states or dream sequences; instead let them sit plainly within the material world of the story so the narrator and characters treat them as normal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrast with fabulism: general magical elements vs direct mythic borrowings
rubrics_metrics.description: Fabulism often borrows and incorporates details from specific myths, fairy tales, and folktales to offer allegorical/moral lessons; magical realism typically uses more general magical elements rather than direct retellings tied to a single known story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If aiming for fabulism, explicitly draw on known fables/myths and moral exempla; for magical realism, weave in fantastical occurrences that feel organic to the setting rather than explicit retellings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance and integration of supernatural (no hierarchy between codes)
rubrics_metrics.description: In magical realism the supernatural is presented as equally valid to the natural; there is no hierarchy between the two codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portray supernatural events with the same narrative authority and matter-of-factness as mundane events so readers have no narratively enforced reason to privilege natural explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorial reticence that normalizes the supernatural
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of authorial reticence: rather than explaining or dramatizing the source of the uncanny, the narration often refrains from over-explaining, which helps integrate the supernatural into the natural framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist extensive exposition or rationalization of the magical; let details be reported plainly and let ambiguity remain so the miraculous becomes an accepted part of the story world.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of hesitation between natural and supernatural explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike fantastic literature, which produces a faltering between belief and non-belief (hesitation whether to attribute events to natural or supernatural causes), magical realism presents the marvelous without that hesitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not stage the narrative around deciding whether an event is 'real' or 'supernatural'; instead convey events as matter-of-fact, so the reader accepts the marvelous as part of reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounding in a realistic, recognizable setting (do not build wholly alternate worlds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Magical realism is set in a world recognizable in relation to past or present reality rather than creating a wholly different world; it suggests the magical in our world rather than inventing a new world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anchor details—social, historical, geographic, domestic—in recognizable reality; let magical elements interrupt or co-exist with this realism rather than replacing it with full world-building of a fantasy realm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roh's visual-art criterion: extreme realism of mundane subject to reveal interior mystery
rubrics_metrics.description: Roh described a style that brings extreme realism to the depiction of mundane subject matter, revealing an 'interior' mystery rather than imposing overtly magical features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In visual or descriptively visual writing, aim for painstaking, faithful rendering of exterior details so 'magic' emerges from the intensity of depiction, not from explicit fantastical adornments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magic-realist painting aspects: ordinary subjects, forward movement vs distance, miniature details
rubrics_metrics.description: Other important aspects include: a return to ordinary subjects as opposed to fantastical ones; a juxtaposition of forward movement with a sense of distance (as opposed to Expressionism's foreshortening); and a use of miniature details even in expansive works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When describing scenes, favor everyday subject matter rendered with careful (sometimes minute) detail and compositional tensions that produce estrangement rather than dramatic distortion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of overt fantastical elements (historical variation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Early formulations (Roh) exclude overtly fantastic features and emphasize faithful realism; later (mid-20th century and after) 'magic realism' in visual art and literature sometimes incorporates overtly fantastic or surreal elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide where on this spectrum your work sits: a Roh-like approach emphasizes strenuously faithful realism that yields a 'magic' effect, whereas later approaches may freely add noticeable fantastical components; both are historically attested but produce different reader responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magical realism in film: matter-of-fact presentation and narrative framing
rubrics_metrics.description: In film, magical realist characteristics are often presented matter-of-factly and occur without explanation; cinematic tools (e.g., first-person framing, child POV, color contrast, historical gaps) are used to establish the magical-realist storytelling frame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In screenwriting/film, avoid special-effects-as-spectacle exposition; instead let camera, POV, color, and narrative frame normalize marvels—examples include Like Water for Chocolate and films by directors noted for magic-realist elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magic realism in games and new media: blending realistic systems with ambiguous magical elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Video games and interactive media can be magic-realist when they combine realistic settings/systems with ambiguous, magical or surreal elements that are not explained away and that interact with the game's 'realistic' mechanics or history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In interactive media, use realistic rules/systems but introduce events or narrative threads that blur the boundary between realism and the marvelous (examples: Kentucky Route Zero, certain Metal Gear entries).
